rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Game Overview 2 Sequence of a Round 3 Allowed Actions 4 Tie-breaking 5 Poker Combinations Game Overview In this cooperative poker game , you take on the roles of a gang of bank robbers trying to crack the combination locks of three safes one after another through perfect coordination and blind intuition. You are not allowed to speak freely; instead, you communicate via chips to collectively assess who has which card combination. You may not share information about your hand with the other players. You may only speculate on the hands of the other players with information that is available to everyone (you may not share any information that relates to your own hand). At the end of each round, the poker hands of all players should be revealed in the correct order from weakest to strongest to crack a safe and avoid triggering an alarm. Goal of the game: Crack 3 safes before 3 alarms are triggered. NOTE: The 1 chip is for the WEAKEST hand. By taking the 1 chip, you are signaling that you believe you have the weakest hand. NOTE: Aces are high, except in a straight, where it can be either high or low. Sequence of a Round A round consists of 4 phases and a showdown : Phase 1 (Hand cards or pre-flop): Everyone receives two face-down cards. Everyone simultaneously takes a white chip , signaling the estimated strength of their current hand. The 1 chip is for the weakest hand, the highest chip is for the strongest hand. The highest 2-card hand is a pair. Phase 2 (The Flop): Three community cards are dealt face-up. You reassess your hand in combination with the community cards, and take/exchange the yellow chips to indicate the CURRENT strength of your hand. Phase 3 (The Turn): A fourth community card is revealed. You take/exchange the orange chips to indicate the CURRENT strength of your hand. Phase 4 (The River): The fifth community card is revealed. You take/exchange the red chips to indicate the CURRENT strength of your hand. Showdown: Hands are revealed one-by-one from lowest ( red ) chip to highest. The poker hands shown must be of equal strength or increasing . Success: Each revealed combination is equal to or stronger than the previous one. → Reveal a safe. Failure: A combination is weaker than one already shown. → Trigger an alarm. Allowed Actions All players play simultaneously . Each player may have only 1 chip per color . You may take a chip from the center or from other players . You may put a chip you have taken back into the center . You must not talk about your own hand cards (not even in chat). You may only discuss information that is clearly visible to everyone. Tie-breaking In the case of identical combinations: Higher main value (e.g., higher pair/three of a kind). Then side cards (kickers) from high to low. Exactly the same 5 cards = a true tie → order does not matter. Poker Combinations Name Example Description In a tie Royal Flush 10♠ J♠ Q♠ K♠ A♠ Straight Flush Straight A-K-Q-J-10 in one suit. Draw. Straight Flush 4♥ 5♥ 6♥ 7♥ 8♥ Straight Flush Five cards in sequence, all in the same suit. Highest card wins. Four of a Kind 8♠ 8♥ 8♣ 8♦ 2♠ Four of a Kind Four cards of the same rank Higher four of a kind wins. Full House J♠ J♣ J♥ 9♠ 9♥ Full House Three of a kind with a pair Higher three of a kind wins; otherwise higher pair. Flush 4♥ J♥ 8♥ 2♥ 9♥ Flush Five cards of the same suit, but not in sequence Highest card of the flush wins. Straight 9♥ 8♣ 7♦ 6♦ 5♠ Straight Five cards in a sequence, but not of the same suit Highest card of the straight wins. Three of a Kind 7♦ 7♠ 7♣ 3♥ A♦ Three of a Kind Three cards of the same rank Higher three of a kind wins. Two Pair 4♠ 4♥ 3♦ 3♣ 6♥ Two Pair Two different pairs Highest pair; then second pair; then kicker. Pair A♣ A♥ 7♣ Q♠ K♥ Pair Two cards of the same rank Higher pair wins; otherwise side card (kicker). High Card 3♥ A♠ 5♣ K♥ 2♦ High Card (Ace) When you have none of the above, the highest card in your hand is the determiner. Compare second highest card (then third, fourth).

So the end result is just okay, I guess. I mean it's definitely not anywhere near as good as The Mind, but it's not even as good as The Crew either, which has a little more complexity to make it work. [Rating: 1/10] Would not recommend for neurospicy folks who like poker. Unfortunately, the cooperative, hidden play made this more frustrating than anything else.

[Rating: 1/10] It feels similar to activities like The Mind, just look at your cards, guesstimate whether you'll be higher or lower than your fellow players, and then somehow manage to rank yourself, but then with poker elements added. If you like activities like The Mind, or enjoy poker but wish you could play it cooperatively, perhaps you might like this, but if you dislike The Mind and/or poker, stay away from this, it being cooperative won't make it any better

[Rating: 1/10] The non-terminal chips do not necessarily show players' confidence in their hands: players can mean anything as long as they come up with a protocol. The rule book is suggesting a strategy rather than a rule, which makes me doubt the logic of the designer.  For example, each player can pick a chip to indicate the suit of the first card, then return it, and keep doing this to give more information.   It is very disappointing to see that this game even has a higher score than Hanabi, whose communication is limited by hint tokens.

[Rating: 2/10] "The Gang" is Texas Hold ’em but with bluffing removed, competition removed and communication limits added. It's basically just a worse version of poker.

[Rating: 2/10] Nearly every hand comes down to assessing the order of player's cards, since meeting the better hands is so rare. This makes the game effectively just feel like The Mind, but with useless extra complexity.

[Rating: 2/10] The Gang has a cool theme but ends up feeling flat and repetitive. Lack of meaningful choices and minimal tension make it forgettable after just a few plays.

[Rating: 2/10] It's pretty much the same game as The Mind.  In The Mind, you play cards in numerical order from low to high by guessing whether you have the next lowest card at the table.  In The Gang, you do the same thing but with poker hands.  In The Mind, you are dealt all your cards at the beginning; in The Gang, there's a useless 4 round structure in which you are first dealt 2 cards, then see 3 face up, then see 1 more face up, then see 1 more face up.  But nothing matters until you have all 7 cards, so the game is drawn out obnoxiously.  Now, I don't love The Mind - it's just a game of intuition - bu

[Rating: 2/10] Yet another limited communication cooperative game, but this time with POKER!   The fun of poker is the high stakes bluffing, which is lacking here.

[Rating: 2/10] If somebody at the table is a poker expert, the team will do very well.   I was impressed how much the poker experts were able to infer about our hands.   But there is nothing fun for players to do in this game.   It's painful.

[Rating: 2/10] Does not scale with player count. With a small number of players it can kind of work, but it was clearly not play tested with large groups. In three separate sessions of 1-2 hours each, we only beat the game once despite using strict logic rulesets. Clearly the game is a 50/50 toss up for if you get lucky. If you enjoy feeling like there was skill involved when it didn’t actually matter, this game is for you. If you enjoy actual strategy or communication based games, this fails on all accounts.

[Rating: 2/10] I don't get the hype for this. One of those rare games that actually made me feel angry, both with myself and other players, which I never get with games. I'll stick to regular Texas Hold 'em!

[Rating: 2/10] Very boring experience. Don't know if the game is so bad or it is just not for me. Probably both.
